title: 6. Numeracy & Number Systems: Place Value in Base Ten
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of a digit in a two-digit number.
questions.question: In the number \(47\), what is the value of the digit \(4\)?
questions.explanation: In \(47\), the digit \(4\) is in the tens place. A digit in the tens place has a value equal to that digit multiplied by \(10\), so \(4\) tens have a value of \(4\times 10=40\). Therefore, the value of the digit \(4\) is \(40\).
questions.hint: Identify the place of the digit first, then use that place to find its value.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the digit in the ones place of a two-digit number.
questions.question: In the number \(58\), which digit is in the ones place?
questions.explanation: In a two-digit number, the digit on the right is in the ones place. In \(58\), the rightmost digit is \(8\), so the digit \(8\) is in the ones place.
questions.hint: In a two-digit number, one digit shows the tens and the other shows the ones. Decide which position is which.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the expanded form of a two-digit number using place value.
questions.question: Which expression shows \(63\) in expanded form?
questions.explanation: In \(63\), the digit \(6\) is in the tens place, so it has a value of \(60\). The digit \(3\) is in the ones place, so it has a value of \(3\). Writing these values as a sum gives \(60+3\). Therefore, the expanded form of \(63\) is \(60+3\).
questions.hint: Separate the number into its tens value and ones value.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of a digit in a three-digit number.
questions.question: In the number \(352\), what is the value of the digit \(5\)?
questions.explanation: In \(352\), the digit \(5\) is in the tens place. A digit in the tens place has a value equal to that digit multiplied by \(10\), so \(5\) tens have a value of \(5\times 10=50\). Therefore, the value of the digit \(5\) is \(50\).
questions.hint: Find the place of the digit, then multiply the digit by the value of that place.

questions.learningObjective: Compose a three-digit number from a given place-value description.
questions.question: A number has \(7\) hundreds, \(0\) tens, and \(4\) ones. What number is it?
questions.explanation: Use the place-value description to build the number. The hundreds digit is \(7\), the tens digit is \(0\), and the ones digit is \(4\). Placing these digits in order gives \(704\). Therefore, the number is \(704\).
questions.hint: Write the hundreds digit, then the tens digit, then the ones digit.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret the role of zero as a placeholder in a three-digit number.
questions.question: In the number \(305\), what does the digit \(0\) represent?
questions.explanation: In \(305\), the digits are in the hundreds, tens, and ones places from left to right. The middle digit \(0\) is in the tens place, so it represents \(0\) tens. Therefore, the digit \(0\) represents \(0\) tens.
questions.hint: Read the number from left to right and identify the place of the middle digit.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the place and value of a digit in a three-digit number.
questions.question: In the number \(480\), the digit \(8\) is in which place, and what is its value?
questions.explanation: In \(480\), the digit \(8\) is the middle digit, so it is in the tens place. A digit in the tens place has a value equal to that digit multiplied by \(10\). Therefore, the value of \(8\) in the tens place is \(8\times 10=80\).
questions.hint: Identify the place of the digit first, then multiply the digit by the value of that place.

questions.learningObjective: Compare the values of the same digit in different places within a number.
questions.question: In the number \(626\), the value of the first \(6\) is how many times the value of the second \(6\)?
questions.explanation: In \(626\), the first \(6\) is in the hundreds place, so its value is \(600\). The second \(6\) is in the ones place, so its value is \(6\). Comparing the two values gives \(600\div 6=100\). Therefore, the value of the first \(6\) is \(100\) times the value of the second \(6\).
questions.hint: Find the value of each \(6\) according to its place, then compare the two values.

questions.learningObjective: Compose a number from its expanded form when the addends are not written in place-value order.
questions.question: Which number equals \(7+400+30\)?
questions.explanation: The addends are not written in place-value order, so match each one to its place: \(400\) is \(4\) hundreds, \(30\) is \(3\) tens, and \(7\) is \(7\) ones. Writing the digits from hundreds to ones gives \(437\). Writing the digits in the order the addends appear (\(743\)) would be incorrect. Therefore, \(7+400+30=437\).
questions.hint: Match each addend to its place (hundreds, tens, ones) before writing the digits; the order of the addends does not matter.

questions.learningObjective: Determine how many tens are in a three-digit number by regrouping.
questions.question: How many tens are in \(250\) altogether?
questions.explanation: The number \(250\) can be regrouped into tens. Since \(10\) ones make \(1\) ten, \(250\) can be written as \(25\times 10\). Therefore, \(250\) contains \(25\) tens altogether.
questions.hint: Think about how many groups of \(10\) are in the whole number.
